w10_P4_003242: A test carriage on a linear rig has a mass of 130000 g. A cam drives a follower whose displacement is 4 times the cube of the elapsed time in seconds, with a coefficient of 0 on the square of the time, and the rate at which that displacement is changing at 2.0 s is taken as the carriage acceleration in metres per second squared. The control computer works out the force needed to give the carriage that acceleration. Because 10 carriages sit on one beam, and 4 such beams share a base plate, the base-plate force is that value multiplied by 10 and then by 4. A tie-down bolt adds a further 12 N to the base plate. If the whole base-plate assembly is duplicated across 10 bays and the loads add, what is the total force, in N?
w10_P4_003247: The reading the technician finally records is 13 kJ less than the kilojoule figure described below. A test puck of mass 26000 g is launched along a level air table, and the launch controller adds its two dial settings 7 and 6 and doubles the sum to fix the launch speed in metres per second. The energy the puck carries because of its motion is measured, and a trigger coil adds a further 22 J to that measurement. The combined figure is then expressed in kilojoules. The air table is fed at 4 bar. What reading does the technician record, in kJ?
w10_P4_003249: A depot stores 113 spare axles and 295 spare bearings, and both stocks are issued in equal batches of the largest size that leaves nothing over in either store. That batch size is multiplied by 11 and then by 7, and the result is used as the acceleration, in metres per second squared, of a shuttle wagon whose mass is 194000 g. The controller works out the force the drive must apply to the wagon to give it that acceleration. A coupling preload of 6 N is added to that force. The depot runs 6 identical shuttles from one drawbar and their loads add. What is the total drawbar force, in N?
w10_P4_003250: The value the crane display shows at the end is 28 kN more than a figure that is itself 27 kN less than the kilonewton reading described below. A hoist controller sets its acceleration, in metres per second squared, to the smaller of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 14x + 48 = 0. A test weight of mass 59 kg is lifted with that acceleration and the force the cable must exert on the weight is calculated. That force, expressed in kilonewtons, is the reading the chain above starts from. What does the crane display show, in kN?
w10_P4_003254: The number printed at the bottom of the run sheet is 26 J more than a figure that is itself 25 J more than the energy described below. A test cart of mass 13000 g rolls along a level bench. Its release speed in metres per second is found from a cam whose displacement is 4 times the cube of the elapsed time, with a coefficient of 0 on the square of the time: read how fast that displacement is changing at 1.0 s, add 26 to the number obtained, and then subtract 29. The energy the cart carries because of its motion at that speed is the energy the chain above starts from. What number is printed at the bottom of the run sheet, in J?
w10_P4_003260: The figure the rig totals up at the end is 5 times a value that is itself 3 times the energy tally described below. On a machine bench a cam gives the follower position as 3 times the cube of the crank angle plus 2 times the square of the crank angle, and the rate at which that position changes at a crank angle of 1.0 is taken as the release speed, in metres per second, of a slider whose mass is 6 kg. The energy the slider carries because of its motion is recorded. The bench fires 11 identical sliders in a cycle, so the cycle energy is 11 times that value, and a resistive heater then adds a further 23 J to the cycle. That cycle tally is the energy the chain above starts from. What figure does the rig total up, in J?
w10_P4_003261: During the first 3 seconds of a discharge, a piston moves at a rate equal to 1 times the square of the elapsed time plus 6 times the elapsed time. The total distance the piston covers from the 0th to the 3rd second, taken as a plain number, is used as the release speed in metres per second of a projectile of mass 6000 g on the adjacent launcher. The energy the projectile carries because of its motion is recorded. The launcher fires 5 projectiles per magazine and 7 magazines are emptied in the trial, and all the energies add. The barrel is 1.2 m long. What is the total energy for the trial, in kJ?
w10_P4_003267: A warehouse holds 374 pallets and 48 cages, and both are moved in equal-sized loads of the largest size that leaves nothing over in either stock. That load size is multiplied by 9, and 29 is then added to the result, to give the release speed in metres per second of a test trolley on the loading rail. The trolley has a mass of 17 kg and runs on a level track. The energy the trolley carries because of its motion at that speed is recorded by the bench logger. What is that energy, in kJ?
w10_P4_003269: A cam on a lab rig gives the follower displacement as 2 times the cube of the shaft angle plus 3 times the square of the shaft angle. How fast that displacement is changing at a shaft angle of 3.0 is used as the acceleration, in metres per second squared, of a slide whose mass is 41 kg. The force needed to accelerate the slide at that rate is calculated and expressed in kilonewtons. A spring preload adds 7 kN to it and a release mechanism then removes 29 kN. The rig has 5 identical slides and their loads add. The shaft is driven by a 400 W motor. What is the combined load, in kN?
w10_P4_003271: A junction box has 7 identical terminals and any 2 of them may be bridged at once; the number of different pairs that can be bridged is used as the acceleration, in metres per second squared, of a test mass of 157 kg on the bench beside it. The force needed to accelerate the test mass at that rate is calculated, and a 1 N tare from the load cell is added to it. That figure is multiplied by 10 because 10 identical masses hang from the same beam. The whole beam assembly is then repeated across 12 bays and the loads add. The box is rated at 24 V. What is the total load, in N?
w10_P4_003272: A store holds 121 clamps and 223 studs, and both are issued in equal batches of the largest size that leaves nothing over in either stock. Adding 4 to that batch size gives the release speed, in metres per second, of a test puck of mass 3000 g on a level air table. The energy the puck carries because of its motion is recorded. The trial is run with 3 pucks at a time, and 10 such trials are carried out, so the total is that energy multiplied by 3 and then by 10. A calibration offset of 12 J is finally subtracted. The table surface is 0.9 m wide. What is the corrected total, in J?
w10_P4_003273: Between the 1st and the 3rd second of a stroke, a pump plunger advances at a rate equal to 3 times the square of the elapsed time plus 1 times the elapsed time. The total advance over that interval, taken as a plain number, has 29 subtracted from it, and what is left is the release speed in metres per second of a test slug whose mass is 60 kg. The slug is released along a level rail and the energy it carries because of its motion is recorded. The rig fires 7 identical slugs in a batch, so the batch energy is 7 times that value. A calibration allowance of 23 J is then subtracted from the batch energy. What figure remains, in J?
w10_P4_003274: A hoist controller adds its two calibration constants 9 and 18, multiplies the sum by 4, and then subtracts 28, treating the result as an acceleration in metres per second squared. A load of mass 66 kg is accelerated at that rate by the cable. The force the cable must apply to the load is worked out and expressed in kilonewtons. The gantry carrying the cable is already under 26 kN of tension from its own weight, and a tensioning jack then adds another 22 kN. What is the total force in the gantry, in kN?
w10_P4_003275: The number the report ends on is 6 times the kilojoule figure described below. A launcher takes its release setting from the smaller of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 12x + 32 = 0, adds 17 to it, and reads the result as a speed in metres per second. A dart of mass 33 kg is released at that speed along a level rail. The energy the dart carries because of its motion is recorded and expressed in kilojoules to give that figure. The rail is 12 m long. What number does the report end on, in kJ?
w10_P4_003278: Between the 1st and the 3rd second of a run, a shaper ram travels at a rate equal to 5 times the square of the elapsed time plus 2 times the elapsed time. The total travel over that interval, taken as a plain number, is used as the release speed in metres per second of a test block of mass 55 kg on the bench beside it. The energy the block carries because of its motion is measured and expressed in kilojoules. A trigger circuit adds 3 kJ to that figure and a damper then absorbs 9 kJ. The machine completes 10 identical runs in a shift and the energies add. The ram stroke is 0.4 m. What is the shift total, in kJ?
w10_P4_003292: The last line of the log is 21 kJ more than 8 times the kilojoule reading described below. A launch controller adds its two dial settings 6 and 9, multiplies the sum by 3, and then subtracts 5 to fix the release speed in metres per second of a trolley whose mass is 13 kg. The trolley is released along a level rail and the energy it carries because of its motion is recorded. That energy, expressed in kilojoules, is the reading the line above is built from. The rail sits 0.75 m above the floor. What is the last line of the log, in kJ?
w10_P4_003293: A cam profile gives the follower displacement as 1 times the cube of the crank angle plus 1 times the square of the crank angle. An engineer measures how fast the rate of change of that displacement is itself changing at a crank angle of 4.0, subtracts 7 from the number obtained, and uses the result as the release speed in metres per second of a slider whose mass is 43000 g. The energy the slider carries because of its motion is recorded. The bench runs 5 sliders per cycle and 4 cycles per test, and all the energies add. The crank is driven at 90 rpm. What is the total energy for the test, in J?
w10_P4_003296: The number stamped on the frame certificate is 8 times the kilonewton figure described below. A cam gives the follower displacement as 5 times the cube of the shaft angle, with a coefficient of 0 on the square of the shaft angle; how fast that displacement is changing at a shaft angle of 2.0 has 12 subtracted from it, and the result is used as the acceleration in metres per second squared of a slide whose mass is 29000 g. The force needed to accelerate the slide at that rate is calculated, and because 8 identical slides run from one frame the frame force is 8 times that force. That frame force, expressed in kilonewtons, is the figure the stamp is built from. The shaft turns at 300 rpm. What is stamped on the frame certificate, in kN?
w10_P4_003297: The figure the bench prints last is 22 kN less than the kilonewton reading described below. During the first second of a stroke, a hydraulic ram advances at a rate equal to 4 times the square of the elapsed time plus 8 times the elapsed time. The total advance from the 0th to the 1st second, taken as a plain number, is the acceleration in metres per second squared given to a carriage of mass 137 kg. The force the drive must apply to the carriage is calculated, and because a second identical carriage shares the same yoke the yoke force is 2 times that force, which is then expressed in kilonewtons. The ram runs at 210 bar. What figure does the bench print last, in kN?
w10_P4_003298: A cam on a press gives the follower displacement as 5 times the cube of the crank angle minus 4 times the square of the crank angle. The rate at which the rate of change of that displacement is itself changing, at a crank angle of 2.0, is used as the acceleration in metres per second squared of a tool slide whose mass is 93000 g. The force needed to accelerate the slide at that rate is calculated and a steady 13 N of guide friction is subtracted from it. The remainder is expressed in kilonewtons, a hold-down jack then adds 12 kN, and a release spring finally takes 14 kN away. The press is driven at 120 rpm. What load remains, in kN?
w10_P4_003303: The number the control panel ends up displaying comes from the chain below, and the very last thing the panel does is add 13 N. During the first 2 seconds of a pour, a ladle tips at a rate equal to 3 times the square of the elapsed time, with a coefficient of 0 on the elapsed time itself. The total tilt accumulated from the 0th to the 2nd second, taken as a plain number, is the acceleration in metres per second squared given to a transfer carriage of mass 143 kg. The force the drive must apply to the carriage to accelerate it at that rate is calculated, then 7 N of bearing drag is subtracted, then a further 13 N of seal drag is subtracted, and only then is the 13 N mentioned above added. What does the control panel display, in N?
w10_P4_003306: A control cabinet has 12 identical contactors and exactly 2 of them close in any one configuration; the number of different configurations available is used as the acceleration setting, in metres per second squared, for a shuttle of mass 98000 g. The force the drive must apply to the shuttle to accelerate it at that rate is calculated and a tare of 18 N from the load cell is added to it. The result is expressed in kilonewtons. Because 2 shuttles run on each rail, and 11 rails share one anchor wall, the wall load is that value multiplied by 2 and then by 11. The cabinet runs at 415 V. What is the load on the anchor wall, in kN?
w10_P4_003311: A depot holds 12 tow bars and 144 shackles, and both are issued in equal batches of the largest size that leaves nothing over in either stock. Subtracting 7 from that batch size gives the release speed, in metres per second, of a test trolley whose mass is 21000 g. The trolley is released along a level rail and the energy it carries because of its motion is recorded. A trigger coil adds 15 J to that figure, and a lamp circuit then adds a further 24 J. The whole measurement is repeated on 2 identical trolleys and the two totals add. What is the combined total, in J?
w10_P4_003314: The figure the report quotes at the end is the kilojoule form of a number that is 4 J more than the joule tally described below. Between the 2nd and the 3rd second of a run, a linear motor advances at a rate equal to 3 times the square of the elapsed time plus 4 times the elapsed time. The total advance over that one-second interval, taken as a plain number, is the release speed in metres per second of a carriage whose mass is 39 kg. The energy the carriage carries because of its motion is recorded, and because 10 carriages run on each rail and 10 rails run in the hall, the hall tally is that energy multiplied by 10 and then by 10 again. What figure does the report quote, in kJ?
w10_P4_003317: The number the rig totals at the end is 7 times the joule figure described below. A cam gives the follower displacement as 2 times the cube of the shaft angle minus 6 times the square of the shaft angle; the rate at which the rate of change of that displacement is itself changing, at a shaft angle of 3.0, has 25 added to it, and the result is the release speed in metres per second of a slider whose mass is 55 kg. The energy the slider carries because of its motion is recorded, and a trigger coil then adds 25 J to it. That combined joule figure is what the total above is built from. The rig is mounted on a plate 0.6 m thick. What number does the rig total, in J?
